subtopic: Issuer Credit Risk and Limits of Principal Protection
source_evidence: they are not risk-free. Any promise to repay some or all of the money you invest will depend on the creditworthiness of the issuer of the note—meaning you could lose all of your money if the issuer of your note goes bankrupt.
question: Misconception: If a structured note promises principal protection, I cannot lose my invested money.
answer: Correction: Principal protection is not risk-free. Repayment depends on the note issuer’s creditworthiness, and you could lose all your money if the issuer goes bankrupt.
